Philip will create a master fallank that becomes the dominant military force in history. He has a childhood friend Aristotle who goes to Athens and learns from Plato. Philip will systemize all Greek knowledge to turn it into an empire tool. His focus is on military conquest but also cultural imperialism.

What makes Philip such a genius is understanding the strengths of different forces: Persians have horse archers, Athenians and Spartans have hoplites. Philip can combine these innovations into one military package for coordination and flexibility. However, to ensure every soldier's motivation, he focuses on increasing morale through meritocracy. If a soldier performs well, they are promoted; if not, demoted. This overturns the social hierarchy, making everyone equally motivated.

Philip uses the anvil and hammer tactics: infantry locks in place while cavalry strikes from behind. This allows him to conquer Persia effectively as no other army had such power. Philip conquers Greece by exploiting internal divisions among city-states. He invades Persia due to its wealth, already having spies and diplomats there.

Tragically, Philip is killed at his daughter's wedding, allegedly by his bodyguard, though some believe it was Olympias.
